reasons: The strategy is not trading the regular-hours opening range the hypothesis requires. The hypothesis states explicitly: 'It must be the regular-hours open.' and 'A rule that trades the weekly reopen is outside the question.' The validation P&L attribution by hour (validation_diagnostics.by_hour_utc) shows the largest single profit hours at 02:00 UTC (+531), 06:00 UTC (+313) and 10:00 UTC (+365) — that is 21:00, 01:00 and 05:00 US Eastern, i.e. deep in the Globex overnight. Combined with a negative hour at 15:00 UTC (-460) and 08:00 UTC (-327) and only ~+97 of the +1040 validation profit falling inside the regular-hours window (14:30–21:00 UTC), the P&L pattern is only consistent with an opening range computed from the Globex session (18:00 ET), not from the 9:30 ET regular-hours open. The strategy builds its opening range from the first `opening_minutes` of `ctx.session` (lines in `_on_5m_bar`) and therefore inherits whatever session the framework hands it; the hourly P&L distribution shows that session is not the regular-hours session the pre-registered question demands. This is exactly the failure mode the hypothesis calls out ('the fourth campaign's best candidate earned almost everything it earned in two hours of Sunday evening, which is the weekly Globex open and not the session open this question is about').

A secondary finding reinforcing the same point: on validation the max_drawdown (-1354.1 points) exceeds the net_pnl (1040.4 points), and the by_month breakdown shows February at -599 against a Jan–May mean of +208 — the result is not stable across the held-out window and is being carried by a minority of overnight hours. Combined with 55 losing sessions out of 86, the headline Sortino of 0.134 on validation is thin relative to the volatility already visible in the same table.
economics.confidence_note: The exact semantics of `ctx.session` and the P&L attribution method (entry hour vs. exit hour) are not given, so the inference rests on the hourly P&L distribution being inconsistent with a regular-hours-only strategy; a framework definition that confines trades to 9:30–16:00 ET would need to be shown to overturn the veto.
